hard_facts: The supplied point-level data covers Wimbledon 2023 men's matches after the first two rounds.
Serving materially affects point and game win probability and must be considered.
External player information is optional but must be fully sourced.
historical_quality_signals: Separates descriptive match-flow measurement from predictive swing detection.
Tests the randomness claim rather than assuming momentum exists.
Uses out-of-match evaluation to discuss generalization.
known_constraints: Test the model on one or more other matches.
Include a one- to two-page coaching memo within the solution.
known_invalid_approaches: Treating raw consecutive point wins as momentum without correcting for server advantage.
Training and evaluating swing predictions on the same observations without leakage controls.
Claiming causality from point-level observational associations.
reasonable_model_families: server-adjusted state-space or exponentially weighted performance model
calibrated binary classification with grouped match validation
runs or permutation testing for the randomness claim
reference_ranges: Predictive quality must be reported on held-out matches with an explicit metric and baseline.
A match-flow score must identify direction and magnitude on a point-by-point timeline.
required_outputs: A match-flow model identifying which player performs better and by how much.
A visualization of match flow for at least one match.
A quantitative assessment of the coach's randomness claim.
A model predicting imminent swings and an analysis of associated factors.
Advice for a player facing a new opponent.
Out-of-match testing, failure analysis, and generalizability discussion.
A one- to two-page memo for coaches.
